rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two seas are the salt oceans and fresh water stored underground, emerging as springs and rivers that flow into the salty sea.
rows.anchor: وأمثل ما قيل في الآيتين أن المراد بالبحرين جنس البحر المالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Underground reservoirs and channels form the barrier: neither sea overwhelms the other, and rainfall and river flow preserve the salinity balance needed for life.
rows.anchor: وبينهما حاجز وهو نفس المخازن الأرضية والمجاري يحجز البحر المالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pearls and coral emerge from both the fresh and salt seas, among their benefits for people.
rows.anchor: أي من البحرين العذب والمالح جميعا وذلك من فوائدهما التي ينتفع بها الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships belong to God despite human construction because their materials, builders, and builders’ abilities are created and owned by Him; He taught people their making and use.
rows.anchor: مملوكة له تعالى مع كونها من صنع الإنسان لأن الأسباب العاملة في إنشائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the earth; every sentient, reasoning being upon it will perish, encompassing humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: أي كل ذي شعور وعقل على الأرض سيفنى وفيه تسجيل الزوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording uses the rational relative pronoun for those on earth because the discourse counts God’s favors to humans and jinn in both lives.
rows.anchor: الكلام مسرود في السورة لتعداد نعمه وآلائه تعالى للثقلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future sense of perishing signals the end of earthly life and the onset of the next life for its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: في الاستقبال كما يستفاد أيضا من السياق يعطي أن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perishing and the advent of the life of recompense are favors, since worldly life is a preliminary stage for the afterlife; this answers the objection that perishing cannot be a favor.
rows.anchor: وكلاهما أعني فناء من عليها وطلوع نشأة الجزاء عليهم من النعم والآلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perishing means returning to God by departing this world, as many verses explain; it is not absolute annihilation.
rows.anchor: حقيقة هذا الفناء الرجوع إلى الله بالانتقال من الدنيا كما تفسره آيات كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thing’s face is what it turns toward others or what others turn toward in it.
rows.anchor: وجه الشيء ما يستقبل به غيره ويقصده به غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s face denotes His noble attributes, intermediaries between Him and creation through which blessings such as creating, governing, mercy, and provision reach creatures.
rows.anchor: صفاته الكريمة التي تتوسط بينه وبين خلقه فتنزل بها عليهم البركات من خلق وتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jalal concerns exalted, repelling or withholding qualities; ikram concerns beautiful qualities that attract, including life, mercy, generosity, and beauty.
rows.anchor: في الجلال شيء من معنى الاعتلاء والترفع المعنوي على الغير فيناسب من الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name ذو الجلال والإكرام combines the names of majesty and beauty, and in truth names the sacred Essence.
rows.anchor: اسم من الأسماء الحسنى جامع بمفهومه بين أسماء الجمال وأسماء الجلال جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description may be detached from its grammatical role for praise, with an implied predicate: He is the Possessor of majesty and honor.
rows.anchor: وهو إما لكونه وصفا مقطوعا عن الوصفية للمدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, face means God’s noble attribute or sacred name, so applying the name to the name ultimately applies it to the Essence.
rows.anchor: لأن المراد بالوجه كما تقدم هو صفته الكريمة واسمه المقدس وإجراء الاسم على الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If face means the divine name, God remains with His majesty and honor, and the creatures’ perishing changes nothing in Him.
rows.anchor: ويبقى ربك عز اسمه بما له من الجلال والإكرام من غير أن يؤثر فناؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If face means what creatures direct themselves toward in God’s sphere, what remains after worldly people perish includes prophets, saints, religion, reward, and nearness to God.
rows.anchor: كل ما ينتسب إليه تعالى فيكون مقصودا بنحو للمتوجه إليه كأنبيائه وأوليائه ودينه

words: لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنسٌ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلَا جَانٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭamth is defloration or intercourse accompanied by bleeding; the passage means no human or jinn had intercourse with the women before their spouses.
rows.anchor: الطمث الافتضاض والنكاح بالتدمية، والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison describes their clear color, radiance, and luster.
rows.anchor: أي في صفاء اللون والبهاء والتلألؤ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a rhetorical denial that explains the gardens and their blessings as God’s recompense for people’s goodness in fearing their Lord.
rows.anchor: استفهام إنكاري في مقام التعليل لما ذكر من إحسانه تعالى عليهم بالجنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that the gardens and their delights are recompense for deeds; it does not address other verses’ teaching that gifts may exceed earned recompense.
rows.anchor: وتفيد الآية أن ما أوتوه من الجنة ونعيمها جزاء لأعمالهم وأما ما يستفاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible inference is that ihsan is complete only when it exceeds what the recipient has done, so the wording may imply an added gift.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يقال الإحسان إنما يتم إذا كان يربو على ما أحسن به المحسن إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two gardens are lower in rank, grace, and honor than the preceding pair, though similar in their blessings; they belong to believers below the sincere God-fearing, namely the people of the right.
rows.anchor: أي أنزل درجة وأحط فضلا وشرفا منهما وإن كانتا شبيهتين بالجنتين السابقتين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the phrase to mean near the first two gardens, suggesting the later gardens also belong to their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى { من دونهما } بالقرب منهما

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some claim these two gardens are better than the preceding pair and that their descriptions are more laudatory.
rows.anchor: بل ادعى بعضهم أن هاتين الجنتين أفضل من السابقتين والصفات المذكورة فيهما أمدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lower-rank reading is stronger in light of the distinction between the sincere, near-to-God and the people of the right.
rows.anchor: وأنت بالتدبر فيما قدمناه في معنى لمن خاف مقام ربه وما يستفاد من كلامه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word describes intense greenness, so deep that it tends toward black; it conveys a tree’s luxuriance.
rows.anchor: الادهمام من الدهمة اشتداد الخضرة بحيث تضرب إلى السواد وهو ابتهاج الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two springs gush forth forcefully from their sources.
rows.anchor: أي فوارتان تخرجان من منبعهما بالدفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruit and pomegranate refer to their trees, as indicated by their parallel with date palms.
rows.anchor: المراد بالفاكهة والرمان شجرتهما بقرينة النخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine plural pronoun refers to the gardens, considered as two gardens in this pair.
rows.anchor: ضمير { فيهن } للجنان باعتبار أنها جنتان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to all four gardens described in the passage.
rows.anchor: وقيل مرجع الضمير الجنات الأربع المذكورة في الآيات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view takes the pronoun to refer to the fruit, date palms, and pomegranates.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير للفاكهة والنخل والرمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr is most often used for moral qualities and ḥasan for appearance; the women are therefore good in character and beautiful in face.
rows.anchor: وأكثر ما يستعمل الخير في المعاني كما أن أكثر استعمال الحسن في الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiām is the plural of tent; the women are protected and secluded, available to no one besides their husbands.
rows.anchor: الخيام جمع خيمة وهي الفسطاط

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ explains rafraf as green garments used to make sitting places.
rows.anchor: في الصحاح الرفرف ثياب خضر تتخذ منها المجالس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here disbelief means rejecting the ruling on ẓihār as a valid divine law; the following command to believe means affirming God’s ruling and the Messenger’s truthfulness in conveying it.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالكفر رد الحكم والأخذ بالظهار بما أنه سنة مؤثرة مقبولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reading takes disbelief as practical disbelief, meaning disobedience.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون المراد بالكفر الكفر في مقام العمل وهو العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥāddah means resistance and opposition; kabt means humiliation and disgrace.
rows.anchor: المحادة الممانعة والمخالفة، والكبت الإذلال والإخزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although verses 5–6 could begin a new discussion of opposition and its effects, the context makes them explain why the preceding verse forbids opposing God and the Messenger.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن تكونا مسوقتين لتعليل ذيل الآية السابقة الذي معناه النهي

words: كُبِتُوا۟ كَمَا كُبِتَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is warranted because opponents of God and His Messenger were humiliated, as were opponents before them.
rows.anchor: الذين يحادون الله ورسوله بالمخالفة أذلوا وأخزوا كما أذل وأخزي الذين من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear signs reinforce that the verses are from God and the Messenger is truthful; those who reject them face a humiliating punishment.
rows.anchor: لا ريب في كونها منا وفي أن رسولنا صادق أمين في تبليغها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase on the day God raises them modifies the preceding promise of painful punishment for disbelievers.
rows.anchor: في يوم يبعثهم الله وهو يوم الحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Day of Judgment God will inform them of the full reality of everything they did in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وهو يوم الحساب والجزاء فيخبرهم بحقيقة جميع ما عملوا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines iḥṣāʾ as securing a count; the term derives from pebbles used for counting, as fingers are used today.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الإحصاء التحصيل بالعدد يقال أحصيت كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s witnessing everything explains how He has comprehensively enumerated their deeds.
rows.anchor: تعليل بقوله { أحصاه الله } وقد مر تفسير شهادة الله

words: قد سمع الله قول التي تجادلك في زوجها
rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that Khawla bint Thaʿlaba complained to the Prophet about her husband Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit’s ẓihār; this passage descended. Al-Ḥākim graded the report sound.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت تبارك الذي وسع سمعه كل شيء إني لأسمع كلام خولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sunni reports are numerous and differ over the woman’s, father’s, husband’s, and his father’s names; the best known identification is Khawla bint Thaʿlaba and Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit al-Anṣārī.
rows.anchor: واختلفت في اسم المرأة واسم أبيها واسم زوجها واسم أبيه والأعرف أن اسمها خولة بنت ثعلبة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view treats the poor emigrants as replacing the orphans, needy, and wayfarers previously listed, or as specifying the needy in that list.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه بدل من اليتامى والمساكين وابن السبيل فيكون ذوو السهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In light of reports from the Imams, the phrase identifies an example of spending in God’s cause, not a separate fixed share for poor emigrants; the Prophet controls the fayʾ and its distribution among the stated recipients.
rows.anchor: والأنسب لما تقدم نقله عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet distributed the Banū al-Naḍīr fayʾ among the emigrants, giving none to the Anṣār except three poor men: Abū Dujāna, Sahl ibn Ḥunayf, and al-Ḥārith ibn al-Ṣimma.
rows.anchor: قسم فيء بني النضير بين المهاجرين ولم يعط الأنصار شيئا إلا ثلاثة من فقرائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor emigrants are Muslims who left Mecca for Medina before the conquest, forced out by Meccan disbelievers and abandoning their homes and property.
rows.anchor: المراد بهم من هاجر من المسلمين من مكة إلى المدينة قبل الفتح وهم الذين أخرجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faḍl means provision: they seek sustenance from God in this life and His good pleasure in the next.
rows.anchor: الفضل الرزق أي يطلبون من الله رزقا في الدنيا ورضوانا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They support God’s cause and His Messenger with their wealth and their lives.
rows.anchor: أي ينصرونه ورسوله بأموالهم وأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse confirms their truthfulness in their profession and in possessing these qualities.
rows.anchor: تصديق لصدقهم في أمرهم وهم على هذه الصفات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view treats the verse as a fresh sentence praising the Anṣār and consoling them for not receiving the fayʾ; the relative clause is subject and their love of emigrants is its predicate.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه استئناف مسوق لمدح الأنصار لتطيب بذلك قلوبهم إذ لم يشركوا في الفيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Settling in the abode is a figurative way to describe building a religious community where believers can take refuge.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتبوي الدار وهو تعميرها بناء مجتمع ديني يأوي إليه المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Settling faith means cultivating it in practice and removing impediments, so its acts of obedience and devotion can be performed freely, as they could not in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وتبوي الإيمان وتعميره رفع نواقصه من حيث العمل بحيث يستطاع العمل بما يدعو إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible parsing coordinates faith with the verb they settled, supplying an omitted governing verb meaning they preferred faith.
rows.anchor: على تبوؤا وقد حذف الفعل العامل فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view coordinates the Anṣār with the emigrants, making the Anṣār participants in the fayʾ.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يشارك الأنصار المهاجرين في الفيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that the Prophet gave some fayʾ to three poor Anṣār supports their participation: if they could receive none, not even three could have received it; the Prophet chose the allocation pattern.
rows.anchor: فإعطاء بعضهم منه دليل على مشاركتهم لهم غير أن الأمر لما كان راجعا إلى النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given that poor emigrants exemplify spending in God’s cause, the Anṣār and later generations are best read as coordinated with the emigrants, not as fresh independent clauses.
rows.anchor: بل ما ورد من إعطائه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم للثلاثة يؤيد هذا الوجه بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that the Prophet gave fayʾ to three Anṣār supports their inclusion; if only poor emigrants had a share, no Anṣār should have received any, while many Anṣār were poor and in need.
rows.anchor: بل ما ورد من إعطائه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم للثلاثة يؤيد هذا الوجه بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the emigrants, and means the Anṣār settled there before the emigrants arrived in Medina.
rows.anchor: للمهاجرين والمراد من قبل مجيئهم وهجرتهم إلى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Anṣār love those who migrated to them because they left the abode of disbelief for the abode of faith and the Muslim community.
rows.anchor: أي يحبون من هاجر إليهم لأجل هجرتهم من دار الكفر إلى دار الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns in they find and their hearts refer to the Anṣār, while the pronoun in they were given refers to the emigrants; min is partitive.
rows.anchor: ضميرا { يجدون } و { صدورهم } للأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Anṣār feel no desire for the emigrants’ allotment and are not resentful or envious of the fayʾ being distributed to them.
rows.anchor: فلا يضيق نفوسهم من تقسيم الفيء بين المهاجرين دونهم ولا يحسدون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view understands ḥājah as the anger or resentment that need can produce.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالحاجة ما يؤدي إليه الحاجة وهو الغيظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īthār means choosing and giving precedence to something over another.
rows.anchor: إيثار الشيء اختياره وتقديمه على غيره، والخصاصة الفقر والحاجة

words: وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ خَصَاصَةٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They put the emigrants ahead of themselves even while poor and in need.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ويقدمون المهاجرين على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم فقر وحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is stronger praise than the preceding trait: they not only refrain from wanting the emigrants’ possessions but give them their own despite need.
rows.anchor: وهذه الخصيصة أغزر وأبلغ في مدحهم من الخصيصة السابقة فالكلام في معنى الإضراب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib explains that a gap in a house is called khaṣāṣ and by extension poverty is a deficiency left unfilled, like khallah.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب خصاص البيت فرجه وعبر عن الفقر الذي لم يسد بالخصاصة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines shuh as miserliness coupled with acquisitiveness in what is customary.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الشح بخل مع حرص فيما كان عادة انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūq is a passive imperfect of protection: whoever God protects from inner constriction about giving or distress at others’ possessions succeeds.
rows.anchor: فعل مضارع مجهول من الوقاية بمعنى الحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whom God protects from the constriction of their souls are the successful.
rows.anchor: فأولئك هم المفلحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about later generations may be a new sentence or may coordinate with the earlier clause about those who settled in the abode.
rows.anchor: استئناف أو عطف نظير ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If read as an independent clause, the relative pronoun is the subject and their prayer for forgiveness is its predicate.
rows.anchor: وعلى الاستئناف فالموصول مبتدأ خبره قوله { يقولون ربنا } الخ

words: فَأَتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا۟
rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam ʿAlī explains that God came upon them from where they did not expect by sending punishment upon them.
rows.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام وقد سئل عما اشتبه على السائل من الآيات قال في قوله تعالى { فأتاهم الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ḥalabī reports from Imam al-Ṣādiq that fayʾ is property gained without bloodshed or killing, and anfal has the same status.
rows.anchor: عن الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال { ما أفاء الله

words: وَلِذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Minhal ibn ʿAmr reports that Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn identified the relatives, needy, and wayfarers as the Imams’ own kin, poor, and travelers.
rows.anchor: روى المنهال بن عمر عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام

words: وَلِذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from Sulaym ibn Qays in al-Tahdhīb attributes the same interpretation of these beneficiaries to the Commander of the Faithful.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا المعنى في التهذيب عن سليم بن قيس عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

rows.speaker: جميع الفقهاء
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says all jurists take the orphans, needy, and wayfarers as people generally; this view is also reported from the Imams.
rows.anchor: وقال جميع الفقهاء هم يتامى الناس عامة وكذلك المساكين وأبناء السبيل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
rows.claim: Zarārah reports that Imams al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq said God entrusted the Prophet with the people’s affairs to test their obedience, then cited the command to accept what the Messenger gives.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة أنه سمع أبا جعفر وأبا عبد الله عليهما السلام يقولان إن الله عز وجل فوض إلى نبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine delegation means God ratified the Prophet’s legislation, made obedience to him obligatory, and gave him authority over people; it does not mean God relinquished His own authority, which is impossible.
rows.anchor: إمضاؤه تعالى ما شرعه النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لهم وافتراض طاعته في ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report from Imam al-Ṣādiq says faith is a house, as are Islam and disbelief.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث الإيمان بعضه من بعض وهو دار وكذلك الإسلام دار

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reports Imam al-Bāqir’s statement that religion is love, citing verses about loving God, faith being beloved, and the Anṣār loving emigrants; he concludes religion and love are one.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة عن أبي جعفرعليه السلام في حديث قال يا زياد ويحك وهل الدين إلا الحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed hadith cited in al-Majmaʿ says miserliness cannot coexist with faith in a Muslim’s heart, nor dust from God’s cause with Hell’s smoke inside him.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع وفي الحديث لا يجتمع الشح والإيمان في قلب رجل مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Faḍl ibn Abī Qurrah reports Imam al-Ṣādiq’s view that shuh is worse than miserliness: it covets both one’s own and others’ property, even by unlawful means, and is never content with God’s provision.
rows.anchor: قال لي أبو عبد الله عليه السلام أتدري من الشحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator brings things into being by determination, the Originator distinguishes them from each other, and the Fashioner gives them distinct forms; the progression is creation, origination, then forming.
rows.anchor: الخالق هو الموجد للأشياء عن تقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous two verses introduce their eleven names with God’s exclusive divinity because lordship and sovereign management entail rightful worship; this verse introduces names of creation instead.
rows.anchor: لأن الأسماء الكريمة المذكورة في الآيتين السابقتين وهي أحد عشر اسما من لوازم الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s exclusive creation does not by itself establish exclusive divinity: idolaters acknowledge Him as Creator while still worshipping other lords and claiming partners.
rows.anchor: لا يستوجب اختصاص الألوهية به كما يدل عليه أن الوثنيين قائلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is the proper name of the Essence that gathers all perfections, to which the other names apply; repeating it at the start of all three verses strengthens the point.
rows.anchor: فهو علم للذات المستجمع لجميع صفات الكمال يرتبط به ويجري عليه جميع الأسماء وفي التكرار مزيد تأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite plural with the article indicates the entirety of the remaining beautiful names.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى بقية الأسماء الحسنى عن آخرها لكون الأسماء جمعا محلى باللام وهو يفيد العموم

words: يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the universe glorifies God, including the heavens and earth themselves.
rows.anchor: أي جميع ما في العالم من المخلوقات حتى نفس السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz means the unconquered victor; al-Ḥakīm means that His acts are precise and never arbitrary.
rows.anchor: الغالب غير المغلوب الذي فعله متقن لا مجازفة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ending with these names signals that the Qur’an comes from the Mighty and Wise, who cannot be defied and does not waste obedience or the reward of the good; this explains repeating Mighty alongside Wise.
rows.anchor: والعناية إلى ختم الكلام بالاسمين والإشارة بذلك إلى كون القرآن النازل من عنده كلام عزيز حكيم
